answer: One defense is a slow-release stake bond: every agent locks a deposit that unfreezes only gradually, like a glacier melting, so spinning up a thousand fake identities ties up a thousand deposits for weeks. Honest agents earn a haven of trusted counterparties by keeping their bond intact and their transaction history clean, while a Sybil that misbehaves forfeits its stake at once. The cost is asymmetric: a velvet-gloved entry for one real agent, but a crushing capital lockup for anyone faking an army.
